findings.title: Fixed-host override validation accepts slots that extend outside the override
findings.body: The override check only rejects a slot when it ends at/before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it, or starts exactly at the override end, falls through and is treated as available. For example, with a fixed host override of 10:00-11:00 and a 60-minute event, an 10:30 or 11:00 slot can be returned for a round-robin event even though the fixed host is unavailable for part or all of it. The check must require the entire slot to be within the override interval, including rejecting equality at the end boundary.

findings.title: Empty date overrides are compared by object identity and do not block their start slot
findings.body: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs objects by reference, so this condition is always false even when `date.start` and `date.end` represent the same instant. Empty/zero-length date overrides (used to represent no availability) therefore fall through; the slot beginning exactly at that instant is considered available because neither subsequent strict boundary check matches it. Compare the instants with `isSame` (or timestamps) and reject the override date as unavailable.

findings.title: Override selection ignores timezone-driven date changes
findings.body: Overrides are selected by comparing the unadjusted UTC-encoded `override.start` date to the invitee day, but their times are subsequently shifted by the organizer/invitee offset. When that shift crosses midnight, the override is applied to a different invitee calendar day than the one used by this filter, so it is omitted entirely. For example, an early-morning Asia/Kolkata override can correspond to the prior calendar day for an America/New_York attendee; requesting that attendee day will return regular availability instead of the override. Filter based on the override interval after converting it to the invitee timezone (and account for intervals overlapping the day).

findings.title: Working-hours validation rejects valid slots for split schedules
findings.body: The code uses `workingHours.find` to find any working-hours interval that does not contain the slot, rather than confirming that at least one interval contains it. With a normal split schedule such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 14:00 slot is rejected as soon as the first interval is examined, even though it is valid in the second interval. This can hide otherwise bookable round-robin slots for fixed hosts. The validation should accept when any same-day interval fully contains the slot, and reject only when none do.
